title: React Testing Core Check
description: Check your understanding of the testing pyramid, Jest or Vitest basics, React Testing Library, component tests, hook tests, mocking, E2E tests, and accessibility checks.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What does the testing pyramid suggest?

options.text: Use many focused unit or component tests, fewer integration tests, and fewer full E2E tests

questions.explanation: The pyramid encourages a broad base of fast focused tests, with fewer slower high-level tests.

questions.prompt: React Testing Library encourages tests that focus on what?

options.text: The exact number of hooks called

questions.explanation: RTL pushes tests toward user behavior, roles, labels, text, and interactions rather than implementation details.

questions.prompt: Which query is usually preferred for a button users can click?
questions.explanation: Role and accessible name queries mirror how users and assistive technologies find controls.

questions.prompt: `userEvent` is generally better than `fireEvent` for modeling realistic user interactions.
questions.explanation: userEvent performs higher-level interactions closer to how a user types, clicks, tabs, and changes controls.

questions.prompt: Which things are reasonable to mock in React tests? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Browser APIs not available in the test environment
A third-party module at a boundary

questions.explanation: Mocks are useful at boundaries, but over-mocking internal components can hide integration bugs.

options.text: When testing a custom hook directly is clearer than testing it through a component

questions.explanation: Prefer testing hooks through components when practical, but renderHook can be useful for isolated custom hook behavior.

questions.prompt: What are E2E tests best suited for?

options.text: Critical user flows across real screens and browser behavior
Testing one pure helper function only

questions.explanation: E2E tests verify complete workflows, but they are slower and more fragile than focused tests.

questions.prompt: What is an accessibility-focused test likely to check?

options.text: Labels, roles, keyboard access, or automated accessibility violations
The exact order of CSS declarations

questions.explanation: Accessibility tests often verify semantic queries, focus behavior, labels, and common automated rule violations.
